headline: Lloyds survey: UK business confidence falls to its lowest in 17 months in September
detail: Lloyds' monthly survey shows British firms at their least confident since April 2025. Executives also took a darker view of the global outlook, with the Iran war reported to be raising costs.

headline: Brent rises more than $1 to $103.73 after Trump denies Iran sanctions relief
detail: Brent crude futures gained more than $1 to $103.73 a barrel in Asian trading after President Trump denied that sanctions relief for Iran was planned.

headline: China announces mortgage subsidies for first-time buyers and cuts a policy interest rate
detail: Beijing is offering support to first-time homebuyers and has cut a policy rate as part of efforts to lift growth, the FT reports. Mainland property stock indices were indicated lower after the announcement, with the Hang Seng Mainland Properties Index seen down 1.3% and the CSI 300 Real Estate Index seen down 5%.

headline: China's official September PMIs: manufacturing 50.1, non-manufacturing 50.2, composite 50.7
detail: NBS manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 from 49.8, in line with forecasts. Non-manufacturing rose to 50.2 from 49.0, above the 49.2 forecast, and the composite rose to 50.7 from 49.5.

headline: Australian August CPI rises to 4.0% y/y from 3.5%, just below the 4.1% forecast; trimmed mean steady at 3.6%
detail: Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m against a 0.5% estimate, while trimmed mean inflation was 3.6% y/y (0.2% m/m) and the weighted median was 3.6% y/y. Building approvals fell 6.1% m/m against a forecast 1.0% fall, and private sector credit rose 0.6% m/m.

headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at its strongest level since 2 February 2023
detail: China's central bank set the yuan's daily reference rate at its strongest level since 2 February 2023.

headline: PBOC injects 833.5bn yuan through overnight reverse repos and conducts no 7-day operations
detail: China's central bank added 833.5bn yuan of liquidity through overnight reverse repos and held no 7-day reverse repo operations, according to its statement.

headline: South Korea's military demands North Korea halt border fortification work and says troops were badly hurt by mines
detail: South Korea's military said North Korea's fortification activity is raising tensions on the peninsula and demanded that it stop immediately and apologise. It also said some of its personnel were seriously injured by North Korean mines.

headline: China's RatingDog September PMIs beat forecasts: manufacturing 52.1, services 51.6, composite 52.4
detail: The private RatingDog survey put manufacturing at 52.1 against a 51.7 forecast and 51.5 in August, and services at 51.6 against 51.3 expected and 51.4 previously. The composite rose to 52.4 from 52.1, and Reuters reported services growth at a three-month high on stronger new orders.

headline: Global bonds head for their worst month in years in September
detail: Reuters reported global bonds weakening on Wednesday, pressured by worsening government finances, heavy issuance and rising inflation. It said energy costs remain high as the US-Israeli war on Iran enters its seventh month.

headline: US forces due to leave their remaining bases in Iraq; Iran's IRGC urges US voters to oust Trump's allies
detail: Reuters reported US troops were due to withdraw from their last bases in Iraq on Wednesday, a departure welcomed by Tehran. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps called on Americans to vote Trump's congressional allies out of office.

headline: South Korean spy agency estimates about 9,000 North Korean soldiers are in Russia
detail: A South Korean lawmaker, citing the spy agency, said there was no sign of further North Korean troop deployments to Russia and that the two countries had cooperated on ballistic missile shipments. The lawmaker also put the chance of North Korea-US talks at the APEC summit at 50%.

headline: China's military runs readiness patrols around Scarborough Shoal
detail: Chinese forces carried out readiness patrols in the sea and airspace around Scarborough Shoal on Wednesday.

headline: Japan's 2-year JGB auction draws a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.89
detail: Japan's Ministry of Finance held a 2-year government bond auction on Wednesday, which drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.89.

headline: China's finance ministry to reopen 80bn yuan of 10-year bonds on 9 October
detail: China's finance ministry said it will sell 80bn yuan of reopened 10-year bonds on 9 October and 20bn yuan of 28-day bills on 8 October.

headline: Poland temporarily shuts Rzeszow and Lublin airports as military aircraft operate; air defences put on readiness
detail: Polish authorities said the two airports were closed temporarily because of military aviation activity. The Polish army said its ground-based air defence and radar reconnaissance systems had reached readiness and that its operational command was monitoring the situation.

headline: Russia says it struck a Kyiv communications centre and energy facilities in the Kyiv region overnight
detail: Interfax, citing Russia's Defence Ministry, reported an overnight strike on a communications centre in Kyiv. The ministry also said energy system facilities in the Kyiv region were hit in what it called a massive strike.

headline: White House holds talks on a possible diesel export ban ahead of the US midterms
detail: The FT reports that the White House is weighing a ban on diesel exports. The report describes a lobbying fight involving President Trump, with oil majors on one side and senior Republicans on the other, who warn of voter anger over high fuel prices.

headline: Vanguard says France's credit is degrading as French borrowing costs rise sharply
detail: The FT reports the warning from Vanguard. It says the Iran war has added to fiscal pressures on Paris ahead of a budget battle.

headline: Dollar is on course for its largest monthly gain against the euro in 14 months
detail: Reuters reports that the dollar is near this year's high against the euro. It cites US growth and rising US interest rates, set against energy and debt concerns in Europe.

headline: Oil prices stay elevated even as Persian Gulf exports recover
detail: The WSJ reports that oil prices remain high despite a recovery in exports from the Persian Gulf. The report gave no price figures.

headline: China imposes an extra 55% tariff on Brazilian beef imports from 1 October
detail: China's commerce ministry said the additional 55% tariff will be charged on top of the rate that currently applies.

headline: Experts put the cost of a fully funded social care model for England at £18.7bn
detail: The FT reports experts saying the prime minister's planned national care service would still leave some elderly people selling their homes to pay for care. They said a model covering all costs would cost £18.7bn and would probably need tax rises.

headline: Kazakhstan restarts enforcement proceedings to recover a 2.3tn tenge fine from the NCOC oil consortium
detail: Kazakhstan has restarted enforcement proceedings to recover a 2.3 trillion tenge fine from North Caspian Operating Company (NCOC), according to an Interfax report.

headline: Gold edges lower as bets on a Fed rate hike and Middle East tensions support the US dollar
detail: Gold prices slipped in early trading on 30 September, with the move attributed to bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike and Middle East tensions supporting the US dollar. No figures were given in the report.

headline: UK GDP grows 0.5% q/q and 1.4% y/y, above forecasts of 0.4% and 1.2%
detail: UK GDP grew 0.5% quarter on quarter against a forecast of 0.4% and a previous reading of 0.4%, and 1.4% year on year against a forecast and previous reading of 1.2%. Business investment rose 1.75% q/q, against a forecast of 1.7% and a previous reading of 1.7%.

headline: UK current account deficit narrows to 19.932bn, smaller than the 25.5bn forecast
detail: The UK current account showed a deficit of 19.932bn, against a forecast of 25.5bn and 22.134bn previously.

headline: Iran's foreign minister takes US feedback on seven-day proposal to Tehran after Doha talks with Qatari mediators
detail: Foreign Minister Araghchi met Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday night and received the US response to the seven-day proposal, which he is due to discuss in Tehran on Wednesday, according to an official briefed on the talks. The official said the main disagreement between the US and Iran concerns sequencing rather than the plan's elements.

headline: German import prices rise 8.3% y/y and 1% m/m, both above forecasts
detail: German import prices rose 8.3% year on year, against a forecast of 8% and 6.8% previously. On the month they rose 1%, against a forecast of 0.7% and 0.2% previously.

headline: German real retail sales rise 1.3% m/m, below the 1.5% forecast, after a 3.4% fall
detail: German real retail sales rose 1.3% month on month, against a forecast of 1.5%. The previous reading was a 3.4% fall.

headline: PM Burnham says the UK should consider options for its EU relationship, including eventually rejoining
detail: Reuters reports that Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that Britain should weigh options for its future relationship with the European Union, including rejoining the bloc in the longer run. He is stepping up efforts to rebuild ties with Europe.

headline: UK Q2 business investment rises 5.2% y/y against a 0.8% forecast; exports up 2.8% q/q, government spending down 0.5%
detail: The Q2 GDP breakdown shows business investment up 1.8% q/q, gross fixed capital formation up 0.9% q/q against a 1.2% forecast, and private consumption up 0.3% q/q, in line with forecasts. Exports grew 2.8% q/q and imports were flat; both had been forecast at 0.5%. Government spending fell 0.5% q/q against a forecast of -0.3%.

headline: PM Burnham says cutting the welfare bill will allow the UK to meet its defence goals
detail: The Prime Minister linked lower welfare spending to paying for the UK's defence spending commitments. No figures were given.

headline: Oil rises after Trump denies he is willing to ease sanctions on Iran
detail: Reuters reports oil prices rose on Wednesday after US President Trump denied he would ease sanctions on Iran, while Qatar pushed for peace talks. Prices had fallen in the previous session as Middle East crude supply recovered.

headline: PM Burnham plans to change the pensions triple lock from 2030 to fund a national care service and admits a possible funding shortfall
detail: City AM reports that the Prime Minister announced the triple lock will be adjusted from 2030, in effect becoming a double lock, with the savings going to a new national care service. He acknowledged the plans may face a shortfall, and economists cited in the report said taxes would need to rise.

headline: Ministers tell business groups the uncapped overnight stay levy will let mayors take on more borrowing
detail: City AM reports that at Labour's Business Day, ministers told leading business groups that the new uncapped tourist tax would allow mayors to increase their borrowing.

headline: UK real household disposable income per head rises 1% in Q2 to £6,577
detail: ONS figures reported by City AM show real household disposable income per head rose 1% in the second quarter to £6,577. The increase was driven by higher benefit payments, which grew faster than wages.

headline: Senior source says seven-day plan needs significant changes before progress can be discussed
detail: Al Arabiya cites a senior source as saying the seven-day proposal needs significant changes before any progress can be discussed. This follows the Iranian foreign minister taking US feedback on the plan back to Tehran after talks in Doha.

headline: Israeli PM and security minister hold urgent talks with senior security officials, sources say
detail: Alaraby TV, citing sources, reports that the Israeli Prime Minister and security minister are holding urgent talks with senior security officials. No further details were given.

headline: French flash HICP falls 0.4% m/m against -0.5% forecast; consumer spending drops 0.5% and PPI rises to 4.8% y/y
detail: Preliminary French HICP fell 0.4% m/m against a forecast of -0.5%, after a 0.7% rise the month before. Consumer spending fell 0.5% m/m against a flat forecast, after a 0.5% rise, and producer prices rose 4.8% y/y, up from 3.4%.

headline: Drone attacks in Russia's Bryansk region kill one person and injure another, says regional governor
detail: The governor of Russia's Bryansk region said drone attacks had killed one person and injured another. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK energy price cap forecast to rise to nearly £2,000 from January as the Iran war lifts prices
detail: The Financial Times reports a forecast that the household energy price cap will rise to nearly £2,000 for January to March. That would be the biggest increase in four years, driven by higher prices linked to the Iran war.

headline: French September flash HICP rises to 3.4% y/y against a 3.2% forecast; CPI rises to 3.0% y/y
detail: France's preliminary September HICP rose to 3.4% y/y, above the 3.2% forecast and up from 2.6%. National CPI rose to 3.0% y/y against a 2.8% forecast, up from 2.4%.

headline: Russia extends its ban on diesel exports to the end of October
detail: Interfax reported on 30 September that Russia has extended its diesel export ban through October. The report gave no market reaction.

headline: PM Burnham says rejoining the EU is an option as the government reviews UK relations with the bloc
detail: The Financial Times reports that the prime minister said full EU membership is an option under consideration. The comments come as the government carries out a review of Britain's relationship with the 27-member bloc.

headline: Iraq's oil exports average 2.65m bpd in September, including 250,000 bpd via Turkey's Ceyhan port
detail: A spokesperson for Iraq's oil ministry gave the September average for daily oil exports as 2.65 million barrels per day. Of that, 250,000 bpd went through the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

headline: US formally ends Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq
detail: The US has formally brought its Operation Inherent Resolve military mission in Iraq to an end. The input does not report any market reaction.

headline: Riksbank Governor Thedeen says the Swedish economy is stronger than expected
detail: Sweden's central bank governor, Erik Thedeen, said on Wednesday 30 September that the Swedish economy has been unexpectedly strong. No figures or policy guidance were given in the report.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield rises above 5.61%, its highest level since 2002
detail: Bloomberg reported that the US 30-year yield went above 5.61% on Tuesday, with inflation concerns and growing bets on Fed rate rises adding to the bond sell-off. The UK 30-year gilt yield stands at 5.307% in the latest snapshot.

headline: Iran gets US response on seven-day trust-building plan through Qatari mediators in Doha
detail: Reuters reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi received the US feedback in Doha on Tuesday. An official briefed on the talks said the order of steps was the main sticking point.

headline: France is the worst-hit G7 government bond market in the sell-off linked to the Iran war
detail: The FT reported that French bonds have fallen more than any other G7 market as fiscal pressure and political risk build ahead of an election. Vanguard said further losses were possible.
